text:
maria: FYI seeing a bunch of flakes on the eval-runner GH Actions job for the quantize branch. fails look like artifact mismatch / wrong matrix pairing :confused:

alex: log? any obvious stack traces?

maria: attaching grep'd snippet from gha logs -> `ERROR: missing shard results for python-3.9/self-hosted`

ci-bot: Build #1245 (eval-runner) failed — check https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/actions/runs/1245 :x:

ben: likely the matrix is producing duplicate job keys when we run on both `self-hosted` and `ubuntu-latest`. artifacts get uploaded with non-unique paths so last-writer wins.

carmen: can we add job-level artifact prefixes using the matrix values? e.g. `artifact_path=${{ matrix.python }}-${{ runner.os }}`. cheap fix.

maria: yeah that helps but we still get flakes where the runner label mismatches and job times out mid-upload. maybe upload is racing with post-job cleanup.

alex: two orthogonal suggestions: 1) make the PR gate run a lightweight smoke eval (fast, deterministic). 2) run the full eval matrix in nightly Buildkite. keeps GH checks fast and stable.

tom: +1. PRs should gate on `eval-smoke` only. Full CI expensive shards -> nightly. We already have Buildkite pools with GPUs for nightly.

buildkite-bot: Scheduled nightly-evals started: pipeline "nightly-eval-matrix" #2023 :rocket:

ben: for the smoke test we should also fix nondeterminism: seed RNGs and write seed into artifact. failing quantization jobs differ by seed sometimes. add `--seed $SEED` and upload `seed.txt` alongside results.

maria: good call. also add `timeout-minutes` to gha job and `strategy.fail-fast: false` so one flaky shard doesn't cancel others.

carmen: example GH Actions snippet I tried locally:
```yaml
name: eval-runner-smoke
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python: [3.10]
      fail-fast: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
      - run: pip install -e .
      - run: |
        SEED=$((RANDOM % 100000))
        echo $SEED > seed.txt
        python -m evals.runner --mode=smoke --seed $SEED --out=results.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: smoke-results-${{ matrix.python }}-${{ runner.os }}
          path: |
            results.json
            seed.txt
```

alex: looks good. for the full matrix on Buildkite we should enable artifact dedupe and add upload checksum. current uploader uses timestamps which vary — use `sha256sum` file to detect duplicates in downstream reporter.

dave: i'll open a small PR to: (1) add `eval-smoke` workflow, (2) modify required checks in repo settings to require `eval-smoke` instead of `eval-runner`, (3) add seed write and artifact prefixing.

maria: thanks. timeline?

dave: aiming EOD today for the PR, staging test tomorrow; if green we cutover Friday.

ben: one more note — GH Actions self-hosted runners sometimes run multiple jobs concurrently and their workspace re-use can cause cross-job contamination. add `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` cleanup step or use fresh temp dir for `pip install -e .`

carmen: i'll add a cleanup step to the workflow. also adding `--exact-times` on S3 cp didn't help but switching to `aws s3 cp --metadata md5=$MD5` plus checking on upload worked well for us.

ci-bot: dave opened PR #312: feat(ci): smoke eval workflow + artifact-prefixing — https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/312 :white_check_mark:

maria: awesome. one follow-up: let's add a short doc in /docs/internal/ about what belongs in PR-gate vs nightly so new contributors understand (smoke vs full eval). I'll draft after PR lands. :memo:

alex: agreed. thanks all — this should reduce the noise and keep PR turnaround fast. :thumbsup:
